accepted.statement: failure of the back-up Inertial Reference System followed immediately by failure of the active Inertial Reference System
accepted.quote: failure of the back-up Inertial Reference System followed immediately by failure of the active Inertial Reference System; - swivelling into the extreme position of the nozzles of the two solid boosters and, slightly later, of the Vulcain engine, causing the launcher to veer abruptly;

accepted.statement: TOC adapter plate not secured with required 24 bolts
accepted.quote: the satellite fell because the TOC adapter plate was not secured to the TOC with the required 24 bolts

accepted.statement: payload fairing failed to separate during ascent
accepted.quote: A payload fairing is a clamshell-shaped cover that encloses and protects a payload on the pad and during early flight. Fairings are a standard component of expendable launch vehicles, and they are always jettisoned as soon as possible after a launch vehicle has achieved an altitude where aeroheating is no longer a risk to the satellite.
A number of ground errors led to the major loss of attitude experienced by the spacecraft.

accepted.statement: Two-phase oxidizer flow and cavitation caused thrusters to trigger fail-off FDIR.
accepted.quote: i. Two-phase oxidizer flow (vaporization and cavitation) ii. Teflon poppet extrusion in oxidizer valves, restricting flow

accepted.statement: thermo-structural failure in the forward dome area
accepted.quote: a thermo-structural failure in the forward dome area of the Z23 motor

accepted.statement: digital logic design error in instrument pyro electronics box
accepted.quote: The root cause of the WIRE mission loss is a digital logic design error in the instrument pyro electronics box.
